claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, Administration placed before City Council or a committee of Council, on a published agenda, at least two distinct proposals to change snow and ice control service, each of whose text states new spending to deliver it. (Primary readings: placed on a published agenda by the comment date; Council or any committee; one service package counts once; the cost must be stated in the proposal's own text.)
claims.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY COUNT. I found three proposals. P=3, C=3, U=0, so the rung is Supported. (1) The 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair' integrated unfunded service package. It is in Attachment 2 of FCS03158 (DocumentId 278877, pp. 27 and 43-44), was on the City Council agenda of 2025-11-24 under item 7.2, and was re-listed on 2025-12-01 under item 5.2 (DocumentId 280346). Its stated cost is 'a $2.11 million one-time capital investment, an annual ongoing operating increase of $1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts in socially vulnerable areas, an annual increase of $1.64 million to enforcement services, as well as $4.59 million for proactive Sidewalk Maintenance repairs'. Its table shows $9,938K net for 2026 and 35.2 FTEs. (2) The 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation' standalone unfunded service package, in the same attachment (pp. 25 and 34) and on the same agendas. It asks for '$100,000 ongoing to contract tow services' and says it 'improves service levels for snow and ice control'. (3) The 'Well Maintained City' service package in report CO03513 (DocumentId 304803) and its Attachment 9 (DocumentId 304812). The Community and Public Services Committee agenda for 2026-08-31 listed it under item 7.1. The brief fixes the publication of that agenda by 2026-08-22 (archive capture, ids 303379-303392). Its stated cost is 'approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding'. Under the primary unit I did not count separately the optional enhancements in Attachment 10 (DocumentId 304813). They are presented as options that depend on the Well Maintained City package, and the report says Council may 'direct Administration to bring forward a service package' for them. Borderline item, left out: the 'Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment to Permanent Positions' package ($1,777K for 2026, 19.0 FTEs). It is a workforce conversion that names 'snow and ice' only as one of the services it supports. Including it would make C=4 and would not change the rung. The rung is robust: even without the parking-ban package (whose classification is the most arguable), items 1 and 3 give C=2. ALTERNATIVES, each changing one choice. (a) Timing rule 'considered by 2026-08-27': Council took items 1 and 2 under item 7.2 on 2025-11-25 (presentations, questions, an in-private session) and under item 5.2 on 2025-12-01 to 2025-12-04. The Well Maintained City package was first considered on 2026-08-31. P=2, C=2, U=0: Supported. If the parking-ban tow package is not read as a change to snow and ice control service, C=1 and the rung is Partially supported. The result is sensitive to that classification. (b) Window to the as-of date of 2026-10-02: no new snow proposal was first placed on an agenda after the comment date in the pages I could read. Item 7.9 on Council's 2026-09-08 agenda re-lists CO03513, which counts once. P=3, C=3: Supported, under either timing rule. (c) Pre-election start of 2025-01-01: CO03079 (Committee, 2025-08-11, item 7.3) is the earlier version of package 1 and counts once with it. CS02945 (Committee, 2025-06-16) is the origin of package 2 and was not read. P=3, C=3: Supported. Under the alternative timing rule, P=2, C=2: Supported. (d) City Council alone: items 1 and 2 were on Council's 2025-11-24 agenda. The Well Maintained City package first reached a Council agenda for 2026-09-08. That agenda followed the 2026-08-31 committee recommendation, so it was published after the comment date. P=2, C=2: Supported. If the parking-ban package is left out, C=1: Partially supported. (e) Unit of separately costed options: the costed options are package 1, package 2, the Well Maintained City package and the 24 costed enhancements in Attachment 10. C is well above 2 (Supported), although a few enhancements (catch-basin equipment, flushers for sweeping) are only partly about snow. (f) Stricter cost reading, requiring the text to state an approved budget and the increase against it: no proposal text in the primary window does this. CO03513, Attachment 9, Attachment 10 and the SOBA package pages state increments but give no approved snow and ice control budget figure. None of them says it can be delivered within existing resources, so I treat their excess as undetermined. C=0, U=3: Not established. If missing baseline text is instead read as failing the test, the rung would be Contradicted. Under the pre-election window, CO03079 states 'The total budget for SNIC is $67 million/year' and 'Funding for these scenarios does not exist within the current budget', so C=1 and U=2. U could move the rung, so the result is Not established. (g) Count rule 'exactly two': primary C=3 gives Partially supported. Under the alternative timing rule C=2, which gives Supported. CONCLUSION: the finding depends on definitions. Supported holds under the primary readings and most alternatives. It does not survive the stricter cost reading, and it turns on the parking-ban classification when the body is Council alone or the timing rule is 'considered'. QUALIFICATION, Well Maintained City package: its own text says it is 'presented here for information ahead of formal presentation during 2027-2030 budget deliberations'. Its report's only recommendation is approval of Policy C409L, for which 'no additional budget is required'. It counts because the brief defines 'put to' as listing on a published agenda. Administration itself describes the formal funding request as still to come. QUALIFICATION, mixed scope: packages 1 and 3 both bundle work that is not snow clearing (sidewalk repair, turf, graffiti, sweeping). Package 1 states a cost specific to snow and ice control ($1.60M ongoing). Package 3 states no split between snow and other work.

limitations: The escribemeetings meeting pages and filestream files returned HTTP 403 to my fetch tool, and web.archive.org was blocked to it. I relied on the carried texts and could not independently retrieve the 2026-08-22 archive capture. I therefore cannot compare the captured files (DocumentIds 303379-303392) with the live files (304803-304817), nor the 2025-11-24 FCS03158 and FCS03159 files with their 2025-12-01 re-listings (280342, 280336, 280337).

Attachment 2 of FCS03158 was carried only in part (sections 9, 13, 20 and 21 of 36). Sections not carried, such as 6-7 (funded packages) and 33 (user fees), did not match 'snow', 'active pathway', 'parking ban' or 'SNIC' under the selection rule, so I assume they hold no snow proposal. I did not read Attachment 1 of FCS03158 (2026 Operating Budget Changes), which may contain funded snow and ice adjustments; the report itself mentions a $2.1M corporate fleet inflation adjustment touching 'snow and ice control', which is not a service change.

Reports I could not read that might hold further snow proposals: CS03123 (Committee 2026-01-19, item 7.1, a traffic bylaw amendment with a Snow and Ice Control Communications Survey attached); CS03508 and CS03544 (Committee 2026-08-31, items 7.2 and 7.3, parking enforcement); CS02945 (Committee 2025-06-16, source of the parking-ban package). Under the primary readings, extra proposals could only raise C, so they cannot lower the rung. I did not search the portal calendar for the whole period because the portal blocked my tool, so other meetings are unsearched.

The Council agenda of 2025-11-24 marks items 7.1 and 7.2 as 'Addendum', and the minutes list them as additions at agenda adoption. The exact publication date is not fixed, so I used the meeting date of 2025-11-24 as the latest possible date. This is still well inside the window.

Reviewer's calculation: for the active pathway package, $1.60M + $1.64M + $4.59M = $7.83M ongoing, while the 2026 table shows $9,938K. The difference, $9.938M - $7.83M = $2.108M, roughly equals the stated $2.11M one-time capital. This suggests the 2026 operating table includes the one-time amount even though the package is labelled 'Ongoing'. An article would need to flag this.
The SNIC-only portion of the package went from $1.94M ongoing (CO03079 Option 3) to $1.60M ongoing in the SOBA package; the package says its amounts 'have been updated'.
The Well Maintained City cost of $23.6M ongoing and $11.5M one-time covers non-snow work as well (turf, graffiti, sweeping, inspections), and no snow-only split is stated.

Parked-claim context, with no verdict assigned by the brief: CO03513 lists 'Calcium Chloride System Upgrades' at $2.5M ongoing and $4.4M one-time. The Committee motions of 2026-08-31 do not name calcium chloride. I did not read Attachment 11.

claims.suggested_one_line: Yes, by the agenda record: by Aug. 27, 2026, Administration had put at least three costed snow-related proposals before Council or its committee: two Fall 2025 unfunded service packages and the $23.6-million-a-year 'Well Maintained City' package. None was funded, and the result depends on which definitions are used.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported under the brief's primary readings. Council's Nov. 24, 2025 agenda carried two unfunded snow-related service packages from Administration: active pathway snow clearing and sidewalk repair ($9.9M in 2026, including $1.6M ongoing for snow clearing), and parking-ban towing ($100K a year). Neither was funded. The committee agenda for Aug. 31, 2026, published by Aug. 22, carried the 'Well Maintained City' package (about $23.6M a year plus $11.5M one-time), which Administration called 'for information' ahead of the 2027-2030 budget, along with 24 costed optional enhancements. The finding depends on definitions: no proposal in the window shows its cost against an identified approved snow budget, and counting Council alone or only items already debated depends on whether the towing package counts as a snow service change.
suggested_tldr: Fall 2025 budget adjustment: two unfunded snow-related packages before Council (active pathway clearing about $9.9M in 2026; parking-ban towing $100K a year); neither was funded.
Aug. 31, 2026 committee: the 'Well Maintained City' package (about $23.6M a year plus $11.5M one-time) and 24 costed optional enhancements, presented ahead of the 2027-2030 budget.
